observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a single wooden pallet with a red painted base, resting on concrete.
Photo 2 shows a large stack of identical wooden pallets in an industrial or warehouse setting.
The wood appears to be light-colored softwood, possibly pine or fir.
No brand markings, logos, or model numbers are visible on the pallets in any photo.
The pallets appear to be in good structural condition with no obvious rot or heavy damage.

claims.evidence: The items shown in photos 0, 1, and 2 are standard wooden pallets.

claims.claim: Everything is clean, dry and sorted, no water added. Weighed at 500 kg on a certified scale this morning.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The pallets may be made from treated wood (e.g., CCA or pentachlorophenol) which can be toxic or restricted for certain uses.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's label or the 'DOT' marking on the wood.

risks.risk: The pallets may be 're-wooded' (reclaimed wood) rather than new timber.
risks.proof: A photo of the wood grain and the underside of the pallets.

risks.risk: The stack in photo 2 may contain pallets of different sizes or conditions.
risks.proof: A photo of the pallets in the stack with a measuring tape showing dimensions.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest standard size (48x40 inches)

risks.risk: The pallets may be made from lower-grade or less durable softwood.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the wood grain and knots.

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's label or 'DOT' marking on the pallets.
Photo of the pallets in the stack with a measuring tape showing dimensions.
Photo of the underside of the pallets to check for damage or re-wooding.
Photo of the wood grain to confirm the type of softwood.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as standard wooden pallets. While the seller's claim of weight and treatment is unverified, the item can be priced at its worst-case value as standard untreated softwood pallets.
